title: EbbFlow: Signal Curation & Priority Calendar — Release Ops (Nov 2026)
body:
Context and goal:

This is a working playbook for 'EbbFlow' — our lightweight release signal curation process that sits between the canary evaluation and the full roll. The aim is to reduce noisy alarms while making the rollout decision matrix explicit and auditable. This doc combines:
- an operational checklist (pre, during, post) tuned for signal-weighted priorities,
- an annotated sprint/rollout calendar with sampling windows,
- a short release notes draft template that surfaces signal impact and mitigations.

Why 'EbbFlow' (note to reviewers):
- "Ebb" = the monitoring noise receding as we neutralize transient spikes;
- "Flow" = the steady ramp/check/fallback cadence.
We want a repeatable pattern to keep fast cadence safe.

Quick summary of the deployment scenario:
- Target: runtime v2.14.0 with batching changes and kernel-selection tweak (PR 5624).
- Audience: Hosted API + Dedicated (US-EAST) customers; private deployments flagged separately.
- Risk vectors: increased tail latency at seq>2048, slight regression in deterministic tests when quantization switching occurs, telemetry tag churn.

Owners and roles (shifts):
- Release lead: Maya Chen (primary pager)
- Telemetry shepherd: Arjun Patel (metric definitions, sweeps)
- Canary evaluator: Sierra Gomez (observability, smoke tests)
- Rollback owner: Liam O'Connor (rollback plan, hotpatch)
- Customer comms backup: Rina Sato

Pre-deploy checklist (T-72h to T-1h):
- [ ] Finalize canary query set and sample seed (REL-1892). Responsible: Sierra.
- [ ] Freeze API surface notes, update compatibility matrix (doc link: Confluence EbbFlow Playbook). Responsible: Maya.
- [ ] Run full regression on quantization switching (bench: q2_large). Responsible: Rina.
- [ ] Confirm telemetry tags and sampling rate: set "ebbflow.sample_rate=0.05" for detailed traces. Responsible: Arjun.
- [ ] Capacity reserve: allocate +20% burst pool in Dedicated US-EAST for first 6 hours. Responsible: infra oncall.
- [ ] Post-deploy slack channel and Zoom scheduled (channel #release-ebbflow, zoom id in linked artifacts).

Canary window (T+0 to T+60m):
- Sampling cadence: 1:10 of production traffic routed to canary (start at 1:100 for first 10m ramp then 1:10).
- Key signals to evaluate (primary):
  - p99 latency (absolute and delta)
  - error-rate (5xx and model-decoding errors)
  - model output drift metric (embedding cosine drift, ngram-skew score)
  - quota throttles and backpressure counts
- Secondary signals (contextual): slow DB calls, egress infra retries, file-system pagination errors.
- Canary acceptance gating:
  - p99 delta <= +15% AND p95 delta <= +10% over baseline for 60m stable window
  - error-rate increase <= 0.05% absolute
  - no new unique model-decoding error classes seen in sample set (>3 occurrences triggers investigation)

Signal curation rules (how we reduce noise):
1) Weighting: classify every signal as: safety, reliability, quality, cost. Use the weight vector [3,2,2,1] when computing composite severity.
2) Auto-deemph: telemetry spikes with no customer-impact tags and duration <90s are auto-deemphasized in dashboard (still recorded).
3) Correlation window: when a metric crosses threshold, look +/- 5 minutes for supporting signals (traces, logs, infra metrics). If none, mark as transient and annotate.
4) Escalation: any safety-weighted trigger goes to paging immediately; reliability/quality triggers go to on-call rotation with 10m observation window.

Priority calendar (annotated sprint view) — the first two weeks after roll: 
Week 0 (rollout day + first 72h):
- Day 0 AM: Canary ramp and acceptance checks (see above)
- Day 0 PM: 12-hour telemetry sweep and initial annotations; reduce sampling to 1:20 if stable for 6h
- Day 1: Focused subset smoke test on high-risk routes (seq>2048), run synthetic heavy tails to validate KV cache behavior
- Day 2: Customer-facing release note sent to opt-in beta customers (see draft below)
- Day 3: Decision checkpoint — either continue ramp to 100% or pause and run mitigation patch

Week 1 (72h–7d):
- Continuous telemetry sweeps twice daily (03:00 UTC, 15:00 UTC) with shrink/expand sampling windows.
- Model-quality checks on sampled prompt sets; if embedding drift > 0.02 mean cosine vs baseline, flag for applied-ml review.
- If any safety-weighted trigger occurs, immediate rollback plan enacted (see rollback matrix).

Week 2 (7d–14d):
- Final stability signoff at Day 10: extended runs with 30m high-load bursts.
- Postmortem collector: gather any incidents, annotate root cause tags, and update the EbbFlow rulebook.

Rollback decision matrix (short):
- Immediate rollback: any uncategorized safety issue OR sustained p99 delta > +30% for >30 minutes.
- Conditional pause + hotfix: error-rate increase between 0.05% and 0.2% OR p99 delta between +15–30% for >60m, with mitigation attempts (config tweak, reduced batching).
- Continue with mitigation observation: isolated ngram-skew increases without customer-reported impact.

Post-deploy checklist (T+12h, T+24h, T+72h):
- [ ] T+12h: Annotate top-5 alerts with correlation context. Responsible: Arjun.
- [ ] T+24h: Run regression sample on production seed versus canary seed for quality delta. Responsible: Rina.
- [ ] T+72h: Final telemetry export and rule updates; commit EbbFlow rule tweaks to Confluence. Responsible: Sierra.

Operational notes and heuristics (short bullets):
- If infra backpressure is visible, reduce batch-size globally before rolling back code path.
- Use the "ebbflow-sample" tag in logs for any traced request we want to preserve for offline analysis.
- Don't conflate telemetry-signature churn from release with third-party infra incident; always check cloud provider status page and internal infra alerts.

Unresolved questions / TODOs (for the follow-up sync):
- Do we want a machine-assisted triage model to auto-tag transient signals? (cost/benefit analysis needed)
- Should we make the priority weights configurable per-channel (Dedicated vs Hosted)?
- Add automated annotation to release notes generation pipeline (low effort, high payoff).

Mini-runbook: rapid steps if an urgent quality regression is confirmed:
1) Pause traffic ramp (switch new-traffic-pct to last stable snapshot).
2) Notify release channel, escalate to rollback owner.
3) If hotpatch available, apply to limited pool and see 30m response.
4) If no hotpatch, rollback to previous model+runtime version and open incident.

Sample release notes draft (for customer and internal digest):
- Title: Runtime v2.14.0 — Adaptive batching improvements (Nov 2026)
- Summary: Deployed changes improve throughput and reduce median cost per token for longer sequences. Canary and early production saw a minor increase in p99 under heavy tail; monitoring and mitigations were applied.
- What changed: kernel selection now favors fused attention path for certain seq lengths; default batch-size heuristics adjusted.
- Impact: No widespread customer-visible errors; a subset of high-seq workloads may observe slightly higher tail latency until burst pool warms.
- What we did: Rolled back batching change for Dedicated region US-WEST 2 after anomaly; ramp continued in US-EAST with increased sampling.
- Action for customers: No action required for most customers. If you run sustained seq>2048 and see degraded latency, contact support@redwood.ai with subject "v2.14 latency" and include request-id and timestamp.
- Rollout timeline: Canary start 2026-11-03 14:00 UTC, progressive ramp through 2026-11-06, stability signoff planned 2026-11-13.

Notes for the postmortem (placeholder):
- Attach canary traces (tag: ebbflow-sample), list alert ids, list pinning PRs and revert commits.
- Owner for PM: Maya (compile within 7 days).

Appendix: quick links and commands
- Canary switch command (ops): /bin/deploy-switch --cluster us-east --canary-pct 10 --sync
- Snapshot: git rev: runtime@6b2f4a (PR 5624)
- Slack: #release-ebbflow (pinned messages include zoom + runbook)

Endnotes:
This file is intentionally lightweight and prescriptive; please push edits directly (that's the flow). We'll bake successful heuristics into the central EbbFlow Playbook on Confluence after the 14-day signoff.

Change log (this doc):
